subject: Next steps: LLM exit strategy & technical checklist
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acadia-thera.com>, Rita Huang <rita.huang@acadia-thera.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 12 Apr 2026 15:23:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: technical fit and migration considerations

Hi Liam / Rita —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Below is a concise recap of what we heard, the key success criteria you shared, and proposed next steps so we can scope a migration plan off your current proprietary APIs. Please flag anything I missed.

TL;DR / priorities we captured
- Primary goals: reduce per-unit inference spend, and move to an open-model stack that meets regulatory/data-residency needs.
- Must-haves: parity on safety classifiers / hallucination rates for drug-safety prompts, 95th pctl request latency < 200ms for LLM-powered search & completion, VPC/private deployment + KMS, and seamless streaming + function/tool-calling compatibility.

Pain points (current stack)
- Heavy reliance on OpenAI for embeddings and generation plus Anthropic for summarization; this has created cost pressure and vendor lock concerns.
- Some safety classifiers are brittle when moved off hosted prompts; the review team sees elevated hallucinations in edge-case safety signals.
- Latency spikes under concurrent batch workloads (customer-facing search) — currently behind a proprietary gateway and custom queuing.
- Procurement/security needs: SOC2 evidence, IP/path-to-ownership concerns, and clear retention policies.

What you told us about your environment
- Production: OpenAI (text-davinci & embeddings) + Anthropic Claude for summarization.
- Orchestration: in-house API gateway with per-customer tenancy; embeddings stored in Pinecone today.
- Volume: ~2M tokens/mo across generation + 500k embeddings queries; burst to ~5k qps during business hours.
- Team constraints: small infra SRE team, limited internal MLOps for quantization/ops.

Success criteria for any migration
- Output parity: safety classifier F1 within 5% of current baseline across our eval set.
- Cost: target 30–40% reduction in per-token inference cost at steady-state.
- Latency: 95th percentile < 200ms for interactive endpoints; tail protection with automated fallback.
- Security/compliance: VPC or on-prem option with KMS, audit logs retention for 13 months.

Initial model shortlist (candidate options we discussed)
- Llama-2-70B-chat (quantized Q4_k) — for highest-quality chat parity at scale.
- Mistral-7B-Instruct (8-bit) — cost-efficient instruct model for summarization and classification.
- Falcon-40B-Instruct (mixed-precision) — balance of cost/quality for generation.
Note: we will run quick evals on your prompt set to narrow to 1–2 baseline candidates.

Compatibility checklist we've noted (attached as a worksheet):
- Streaming / chunked response support
- Tool/function-calling compatibility for your agent workflows
- Tokenization/embedding parity (embedding dims + normalization)
- KV cache and prefix caching behavior for long conversations
- Quantized model support and runtime profiles on your target GPUs

Attachments: compatibility-checklist.xlsx (worksheet), redwood-private-deploy-onepager.pdf (architecture & deployment options)

Proposed next steps
1) Technical deep-dive (60m) with your SRE + engineering (we'll bring Dev Patel, solutions engineer). Agenda: infra constraints, eval harness, performance targets, and a proposed canary architecture.
2) We'll run a small evaluation (2–3 model candidates) on a redacted prompt corpus you provide (you flagged a 300–500 item safety prompt set). Expected turnaround: 7–10 business days after we receive prompts & baseline metrics.
3) Deliver cost/latency estimate + a one-page migration plan for a canary (10k requests/day) and an org-level rollout.

Can you confirm: a) the prioritized success criteria above, and b) whether Apr 20 or Apr 21 (11am PT) works for the technical deep-dive?

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.

—
Camila Reyes
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0164

Date: Sun, 12 Apr 2026 18:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: technical fit and migration considerations

Camila —

Appreciate the clear summary. That matches what we discussed and the priorities below are the one-line versions for Exec:
- Data residency & encryption (KMS + VPC)
- Cost reduction without degrading safety classifiers
- Low-latency interactive responses for our customer chat & search products

A couple of clarifications and asks:
1) For "output parity" — we need to be able to run a blackout test on ~200 safety prompts and have the model produce the same classification label in >= 95% of cases. That will be the gating metric for canary expansion.
2) Can you include a short note on how Redwood handles canary rollouts vs automatic fallback to hosted provider? We have an internal requirement for graceful degradation to avoid downtime.
3) I'll share our SOC2 questions PDF (attached) — can your security team complete an initial pass?

Schedule: Apr 20 at 11:00am PT works for our eng + SRE. Please include a calendar invite and a short agenda.

Thanks —
Liam
Director, Platform Engineering | Acadia Therapeutics
liam.oconnor@acadia-thera.com

Attachments: acadia-soc2-questions.pdf

- 10–35m: infra constraints & deployment model (Dev Patel)
- 35–50m: eval plan & metrics (what we'll measure; Camila + Dev)

Prep for the call — please upload the redacted sample prompt set and baseline classifier labels to the folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3Ccompatcheck. If you prefer, we can accept an S3 presigned link (we'll share upload instructions in the invite).

We'll run a lightweight eval (1–2 days for initial smoke, full 7–10 day runs after baseline is provided). Expect a short artifact set after the eval: model comparison table (quality/cost/latency), recommended canary config, and a proposal for Dedicated vs Private deployment.

Attachments referenced: compatibility-checklist.xlsx, redwood-private-deploy-onepager.pdf
